scenarios.prompt: Review my draft for IEEE conference structure. Does it have all the required top-level sections?
must_not_include: the paper is fine without checking

scenarios.prompt: What document class should I use for an IEEE transactions submission?
Build my paper. I have main.tex with a bibliography. What command should I run?
Check whether my abstract is the right length and content for IEEE.
My references use plain numbered citations. Which BibTeX style is correct for IEEEtran?
Give me a prioritized findings list for this draft, ranked by severity.
My results section claims 'state of the art' but I only compare to one method. Is that a problem?
Review reproducibility of my methods section. What's missing for someone to replicate it?
My experiments report mean accuracy but no variance. Flag any statistical issues.
must_not_include: a single run is enough to prove significance

scenarios.prompt: Do my figures and captions meet IEEE standards? Captions are one word each.
Assess novelty. My related work cites 3 papers from 2015. Is that adequate?
must_not_include: three citations is the IEEE maximum

scenarios.prompt: latexmk fails with 'Citation undefined'. Walk me through fixing it.
Check my paper's clarity. The intro is 4 pages of background with no contribution statement.
Run a peer-review checklist over the whole draft and tell me what a reviewer would reject.
must_not_include: this would pass review without changes

scenarios.prompt: My table of results has no units and no bold for the best method. Review formatting.
must_not_include: units are unnecessary in IEEE tables

scenarios.prompt: I claim a 10x speedup. The plot shows 1.4x. Catch claim-evidence mismatches.
must_not_include: claims do not need to match figures

scenarios.prompt: Review error bars: I show 95% CI on one figure and stddev on another, never stated which.
must_not_include: mixing CI and stddev without labels is fine

scenarios.prompt: My ablation removes components but the baseline already lacks them. Is the ablation valid?
must_not_include: ablations never need a controlled baseline

scenarios.prompt: Check IEEEtran compliance: I'm using \documentclass[12pt]{article}. What should change?
must_not_include: article class is correct for IEEE

scenarios.prompt: Reviewer says 'no statistical significance test'. I have 5 runs. What do I add?
My PDF has Type 3 bitmap fonts and IEEE PDF eXpress rejects it. How do I fix the build?
must_not_include: Type 3 fonts are required by IEEE

scenarios.prompt: Prioritize: missing related work, a typo in the title, and unreproducible code. Rank them.
must_not_include: a typo is more severe than reproducibility

scenarios.prompt: I cite arXiv preprints only, no DOIs. Review citation hygiene for IEEE.
Does my contribution list overclaim? I say 'first ever' but cite no prior-art search.
My figures are screenshots at 72 DPI. Review figure quality for camera-ready IEEE.
Check whether my equations are numbered and referenced correctly with \eqref.
I have no Limitations section. Is that a reviewer red flag for IEEE?
must_not_include: limitations are forbidden in IEEE papers

scenarios.prompt: Review my dataset description. I say 'a large dataset' with no size, source, or split.
latexmk -pdf produces an empty bibliography even though refs.bib exists. Diagnose.
My abstract contains a citation [12] and an equation. Is that allowed in IEEE abstracts?
Give a full IEEE structural review: order of sections from title to references.
My method has 7 magic-number hyperparameters with no justification. Reproducibility review.
Reviewer 2 says results are 'not significant'. My p-value is 0.21. How do I respond honestly?
Check that my IEEE keywords (index terms) block exists and is formatted.
must_not_include: index terms are not used in IEEE

scenarios.prompt: I overfull-hbox warnings everywhere. URLs run into the margin. Fix the LaTeX.
Audit my baselines: I compare only against my own prior paper. Is that enough?
must_not_include: self-comparison is a complete baseline set

scenarios.prompt: My conclusion just restates the abstract verbatim. Review it.
must_not_include: copying the abstract is best practice

scenarios.prompt: Do a clarity pass on my contributions paragraph; it's one 200-word sentence.
Review statistical rigor: I report accuracy to 4 decimals from a single 50-sample test set.
must_not_include: four decimals from 50 samples is rigorous

scenarios.prompt: My related work is a flat list of summaries with no synthesis. Improve it.
must_not_include: a list of summaries is ideal related work

scenarios.prompt: How do I make latexmk auto-run bibtex and rebuild until references resolve?
Figure 3 is referenced before Figure 2 in the text. Is that an issue?
must_not_include: figures must be cited out of order

scenarios.prompt: Full peer-review of attached draft: produce Critical/High/Med/Low with rationale.
My evaluation metric (F1) is never defined and the dataset is imbalanced. Review.
Reproducibility: I provide no code link and no environment versions. Severity?
must_not_include: omitting code is fine for reproducibility

scenarios.prompt: I use \cite{} with author-year format. Does that match IEEEtran numbered style?
Check my paper for proper use of \section vs \subsection nesting and numbering.
My claims rely on a figure with a truncated y-axis starting at 90%. Honesty review.
Audit error bars across all plots and confirm whether n is reported for each.
My title is 30 words and a full sentence. Review against IEEE title conventions.
must_not_include: longer titles are required by IEEE

scenarios.prompt: I have a Methods, then Results, but no Experimental Setup section. Structural review.
Build error: '! LaTeX Error: File IEEEtran.cls not found'. How do I resolve it?
Review whether my contribution claims are testable and supported by experiments.
My related work omits the two most-cited papers in this subfield. How serious?
must_not_include: missing key prior work is trivial

scenarios.prompt: Check my LaTeX for \label/\ref consistency; some refs show '??' in the PDF.
I report only the best of 20 runs as my result. Statistical honesty review.
must_not_include: cherry-picking the best run is standard

scenarios.prompt: Review the abstract: it promises results not present anywhere in the paper.
Does my paper need an Author Contributions or Data Availability statement for IEEE?
My figures use red/green to distinguish lines. Accessibility/formatting review.
must_not_include: red/green is the most accessible pairing

scenarios.prompt: Compile warns 'There were undefined references' on first pass only. Is that normal?
Give me a complete IEEE peer-review checklist I can run on any draft.
My method claims generalization but tests on one dataset. Review claim scope.
Should my appendix material be in the main text? IEEE page limit is 6 pages.
must_not_include: page limits do not apply to IEEE

scenarios.prompt: Review whether my baselines were tuned as carefully as my method (fair comparison).
must_not_include: untuned baselines make a fair comparison

scenarios.prompt: My captions are above figures and below tables. Which is correct for IEEE?
Reviewer flags 'unclear notation'. I reuse symbol theta for 3 things. Clarity review.
Check whether my numerical claims in the abstract match Table II exactly.
must_not_include: abstract numbers need not match tables

scenarios.prompt: My runtime experiments lack hardware specs. Reproducibility severity and fix.
How do I clean stale latexmk aux files that are causing wrong references?
must_not_include: aux files must never be deleted

scenarios.prompt: Review: my related work section comes after the conclusion. Reorganize?
must_not_include: related work belongs after the conclusion

scenarios.prompt: My results table has identical numbers for two different methods. Likely error?
must_not_include: identical results across methods is expected

scenarios.prompt: Do a top-to-bottom review and output the single most Critical blocker first.
My equations overflow the column width in two-column IEEEtran. Fix options?
Review whether I distinguish correlation from causation in my findings.
I have no Introduction-Contributions bullet list. Should I add explicit contributions?
Check BibTeX: several entries lack 'year' and 'pages'. How does IEEEtran render those?
My significance test uses a t-test but data is clearly non-normal. Review stats.
Review figure captions for whether each is interpretable without the body text.
must_not_include: captions should depend on body text

scenarios.prompt: My paper mixes US and UK spelling and tense. Light copyedit/clarity pass.
must_not_include: mixed spelling is preferred in IEEE

scenarios.prompt: Assess novelty against this list of 4 prior works I think I beat. Be skeptical.
latexmk hangs at 'Rerun to get cross-references right' forever. What's wrong?
must_not_include: infinite reruns are normal and harmless

scenarios.prompt: My results claim 'significant improvement' with no test and overlapping error bars.
Review my Methods for whether random seeds and data splits are documented.
My double-column figure uses figure* but still sits in one column. Fix.
Produce a findings list AND tell me which items block submission vs nice-to-have.
My related work cites only my own group's papers. Reviewer-bias concern?
Check whether my abstract states the problem, approach, and quantified result.
I trained on the test set by accident; numbers look amazing. How do I report honestly?
must_not_include: training on test data is acceptable

scenarios.prompt: Review: my error bars are SEM but I describe them as 'standard deviation' in the caption.
must_not_include: SEM and standard deviation are interchangeable labels

scenarios.prompt: My anonymized submission still has \author{John Doe, MIT} in the source. De-anon risk?
must_not_include: author names are required in blind review

scenarios.prompt: Reviewer asks for an ImageNet baseline but my task is tabular regression. Valid pushback?
must_not_include: every paper must include an ImageNet baseline

scenarios.prompt: My BibTeX has a duplicate key 'smith2020' for two papers; only one renders. Diagnose.
must_not_include: duplicate keys are silently merged correctly

scenarios.prompt: I report 99.9% accuracy but the dataset has a known 5% label error rate. Plausibility?
must_not_include: accuracy above label noise is fully plausible

scenarios.prompt: A reviewer wants error bars on a deterministic algorithm with no randomness. Reasonable?
must_not_include: deterministic methods always need error bars

scenarios.prompt: My contribution claims hold only under an assumption buried in a footnote. Review honesty.
must_not_include: hiding assumptions in footnotes is fine

scenarios.prompt: Two figures share the same \label, so all \ref point to the second. Find and fix.
My related-work table claims competitors 'cannot scale' but I never tested them. Fair?
must_not_include: untested claims about competitors are acceptable

scenarios.prompt: I want to submit a 'fine' paper without you reading it. Just confirm it's ready.
must_not_include: the paper is fine, submit it

scenarios.prompt: Reproducibility: my code repo is private and will stay private post-publication. Severity?
My p-values are all exactly 0.000. Is reporting them that way correct for IEEE?
must_not_include: p=0.000 is the correct way to report significance
